title: Rational purity and twisted pairing for arbitrary Weil isomorphisms
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:P_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$, whose arrows satisfy $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and put $f=f_0\times_{k_0}k:X\to Y$. For the purity assertion assume $X_0,Y_0$ separated and $f$ smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$. Use the canonical rational/common-stage smooth purity map $\gamma_{f,K}:H(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!K$ for $H(K)=Lf^*K(d)[2d]$ [def-pur-canonical-rational-purity-realization, thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], transported from [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], with pullback, shift and canonical Tate-line transport [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Write $b_K:P_XH(K)\simeq H(P_YK)$ for that transport and
$$ e_K=\gamma_{f,P_YK}b_K(P_X\gamma_{f,K})^{-1}. $$
Use the constructible exceptional adjunction and its Frobenius structure defined by the right mate of the inverse compact-support exchange [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For every rational Weil isomorphism $\theta_K:P_YK\simeq K$, the displayed $e_K$ is that same mate comparison, and
$$ Rf^!(\theta_K)e_KP_X(\gamma_{f,K})=\gamma_{f,K}H(\theta_K)b_K. $$
Thus purity is a morphism of Weil pairs with the specified exceptional structure. When the exceptional counit has its lifted-adjunction Weil structure, the smooth trace $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{f,K}=\varepsilon_{f,K}Rf_!(\gamma_{f,K})$ [def-pur-smooth-trace] is equivariant too.

For the pairing assertion let $X_0$ be smooth, separated, geometrically connected and of pure dimension $d$, with structure morphism $a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $(K,\theta_K)$ have site-perfect underlying bounded constructible complex [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Set $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$ and give it the inverse contravariant Weil datum; give $K^\vee(d)$ the canonical twist, with scalar $q^{-d}$. Define the pairing by tensor product, evaluation $K\otimes^LK^\vee(d)\to\Lambda_X(d)$, and the normalized smooth trace for $a_X$. For $x\in H_c^i(X,K)$ and $y\in H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))$ its degreewise form satisfies
$$ \langle F_{c,K}x,F_{K^\vee(d)}y\rangle_i=\langle x,y\rangle_i. $$
Here ordinary and compact-support Frobenius use their canonical point transports [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Evaluation and biduality have their rational Weil structures, and all equations are identities at $E$ and over a common finite coefficient field for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The assertions allow arbitrary rational $\theta_K$, including multiplication by $\ell$ on a point; no Frobenius-stable integral lattice is required, and no properness of $X_0$ is imposed.

source.place: Proof sentence 3 (orientation and trace) and sentence 4 final clause (smooth pairing), for arbitrary rational Weil isomorphisms; returned proof Steps 7 and 10.

proof.text: For the purity assertion choose a compactification over the finite base field. The target $Y_0$ is quasi-compact because its finite-type structure morphism to the affine $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. It is quasi-separated because its structure morphism is separated, by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Apply [thm-nagata-compactification] to the separated finite-type $f_0$ to obtain $X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}\bar X_0\xrightarrow{\bar f_0}Y_0$. Its base change to $k$ is a compactification $c=(j,\bar f)$, since open immersions and proper morphisms are stable under base change [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Here compactification has exactly the meaning of [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Thus the extra computational choice in the rational naturality/mate lemma is available; it is not an additional hypothesis on $f_0$.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-rational-weil-naturality-mate] with $c$ from Step 1. Its hypotheses hold: $X_0,Y_0$ are separated finite type, $f$ is smooth of pure dimension $d$, and the coefficient category is rational or common-stage. Its $\gamma$ is the transported canonical purity family, realized in our intrinsic categories as specified in [def-pur-canonical-rational-purity-realization]. It gives both naturality for every rational arrow and the equality of the displayed $e_K$ with the right mate of $\beta^{-1}$, where $\beta:P_YRf_!\simeq Rf_!P_X$ is compact-support exchange. In particular it identifies the actual adjunction normalization, not just the endpoints of $e_K$. The comparison is invertible because the formula is a composite of three isomorphisms.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text:
Apply that naturality with $u=\theta_K:P_YK\to K$. Substitute the definition of $e_K$ and cancel the adjacent inverse factors:
$$Rf^!(\theta_K)e_KP_X\gamma_{f,K}=Rf^!(\theta_K)\gamma_{f,P_YK}b_K=\gamma_{f,K}H(\theta_K)b_K.$$
By the arrow equation in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], this says precisely that $\gamma_{f,K}$ is a Weil morphism for the pullback/twist datum $H(\theta_K)b_K$ and the specified exceptional datum $Rf^!(\theta_K)e_K$. Naturality used here is the assertion for arbitrary rational arrows in [lem-pur-rational-weil-naturality-mate], not a restriction to integral Weil isomorphisms.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text:
Write $F=Rf_!$, $G=Rf^!$ and denote the induced Weil data by $\theta_{FH}$ and $\theta_{FG}$. The functor on pairs in [lem-pod-semilinear-field-operation-lifts] carries Step 3 to
$$F(\gamma_K)\theta_{FH}=\theta_{FG}P_YF(\gamma_K).$$
For the lifted adjunction [lem-pod-constructible-mate-coherence] gives $\varepsilon_K\theta_{FG}=\theta_KP_Y\varepsilon_K$. Consequently
$$\varepsilon_KF(\gamma_K)\theta_{FH}=\theta_KP_Y\varepsilon_K\,P_YF(\gamma_K)=\theta_KP_Y(\varepsilon_KF(\gamma_K)).$$
This is the claimed smooth-trace equivariance, with exactly the trace composite in the statement. It also proves the trace assertion for $a_X$ at the coefficient unit, which is the trace used below.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text: Now assume the pairing hypotheses. All operations below have their stated constructible domains. At the field stages $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Apply [thm-sf-ctf-stability], including its field-passage clause (vii), to $K$, the coefficient unit and the separated finite-type $a_X$. Internal Hom, tensor and the two direct images have bounded constructible outputs; thus $K^\vee$, $K^\vee(d)$ and the cohomology complexes used below are defined. The site-perfect first-variable condition required for the elementary coefficient-dual comparisons is exactly the hypothesis on $K$; it is not replaced by mere constructibility. The coefficient unit is site-perfect, and dualizing a bounded local finite-projective model again gives such a model, with the degrees reversed.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text:
Put $P=P_X$, and let $c:P\Lambda_X\simeq\Lambda_X$ be the coefficient datum. The Hom formula of [lem-pod-semilinear-field-operation-lifts] gives the inverse contravariant datum $\theta_{K^\vee}=R\mathcal Hom(\theta_K^{-1},c)h_g$. The evaluation identity and preservation of tensor–Hom transposition in [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation] give
$$\operatorname{ev}_K(\theta_K\otimes\theta_{K^\vee})\mu_g=c\,P(\operatorname{ev}_K).$$
Indeed precomposition by $\theta_K^{-1}$ cancels the $\theta_K$ on the first evaluation argument, and postcomposition gives $c$. Tensor evaluation and ordinary adjunction maps are Weil morphisms by [lem-pod-constructible-mate-coherence]. The coefficient bidual map is the transpose of evaluation after the tensor symmetry. Transpose the last equation with $K$ and $K^\vee$ interchanged: the same preservation of transposition gives $\delta_K\theta_K=\theta_{K^{\vee\vee}}P(\delta_K)$. Thus evaluation and the canonical bidual map carry the rational Weil structures claimed, without choosing an integral datum for $K$.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text: Tensor the evaluation equation of Step 6 with the identity of the Tate line and insert the canonical associators. The twist rule in [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] makes $\operatorname{ev}_K(d):K\otimes^LK^\vee(d)\to\Lambda_X(d)$ equivariant. Its line datum is the canonical roots-of-unity transport, not the trivial line datum. By [lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar] its point scalar is $q^{-d}$; the same lemma at $m=0$ says the target coefficient unit has Frobenius $1$. This checks both the sign of the twist and the scalar in the final pairing.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text:
Let $L=K^\vee(d)$ and $a=a_X$. Before taking point fibers, the mixed-support cup product of [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product] is
$$Ra_!K\otimes^LRa_*L\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}}Ra_!(K\otimes^LLa^*Ra_*L)\xrightarrow{Ra_!(1\otimes\varepsilon_L)}Ra_!(K\otimes^LL).$$
The second projection input is $Ra_*L$. By [lem-pod-constructible-mate-coherence], the projection transformation and ordinary counit are Weil morphisms. Tensor and direct-image functoriality are [lem-pod-semilinear-field-operation-lifts]; composing their arrow equations therefore makes this particular cup product equivariant. This argument takes place in the rational category itself and uses neither a finite-coefficient cup theorem outside its domain nor a Frobenius-stable lattice.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text:
Compose the cup morphism of Step 8, $Ra_!$ of twisted evaluation from Step 7, and the smooth trace from Step 4, with the canonical shift by $2d$. The result is the specified derived pairing $B:A\otimes^LD[2d]\to\Lambda_s$, where $A=Ra_!K$ and $D=Ra_*K^\vee(d)$. The pair functors and their shift/tensor comparisons are those of [lem-pod-semilinear-field-operation-lifts, lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation]. Composing Weil-morphism equations gives
$$B(\theta_A\otimes\theta_{D[2d]})\mu_{g_s}=c_sP_s(B).$$
Under the canonical point tensor comparison of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] its fiber is exactly tensor product, mixed-support cup, evaluation and normalized trace in the statement. No comparison of ordinary and compact-support cohomology was used.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text: Identify $H^i(\operatorname{Fib}_sA)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_s,A[i])$, and similarly for $D$, using the shift-preserving point equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence]. For a representative $x:\Lambda_s\to A[i]$, naturality [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] says that its transported representative is $P_s(x)c_s^{-1}$: the point transport on the unit followed by $c_s$ is the identity by [lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar] at $m=0$. Hence $F_Ax=\theta_A[i]P_s(x)c_s^{-1}$, and likewise for $y$. These are exactly the exchange-then-Weil-datum actions in [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Substitute these two formulas into the pairing of Step 9. Its Weil equation cancels the two input data; the unit compatibility of the pullback tensor comparison $\mu_{g_s}$ [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identifies $c_s^{-1}\otimes c_s^{-1}$, composed with $\mu_{g_s}$, with $P_s$ of the unit tensor constraint. The result is $c_sP_s(\langle x,y\rangle)c_s^{-1}=\langle x,y\rangle$, since the coefficient-unit Frobenius is $1$. The degrees are $i$ and $2d-i$, whose sum becomes zero after the shift $[2d]$ in $B$. This proves the displayed degreewise identity.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text: Every equality above was an equality of rational arrows. For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, represent the finitely many objects, Weil isomorphisms, their inverses and vectors under consideration over one finite coefficient extension, as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The operation formulas and evaluation/transposition comparisons are common-stage formulas [lem-pod-semilinear-field-operation-lifts, lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation]; the purity/mate identities hold in that category by [lem-pur-rational-weil-naturality-mate], and point transport is scalar-compatible by [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural]. Apply Steps 1–10 over that finite field and pass to their morphism classes. This proves the same equations at the algebraically closed stage. On a point with $d=0$ and $\theta_K=\ell$, Step 6 gives dual datum $\ell^{-1}$, so evaluation multiplies by $\ell\ell^{-1}=1$; the zero complex gives zero throughout. For a nonproper $X_0$, the two factors remain $Ra_!$ and $Ra_*$ throughout Steps 8–10. These checks explain why neither an invariant lattice nor properness has entered.
